text:
omar: Quick follow-up from yesterday's postmortem — three recurring-ish issues we need tracked: missing spans in traces, bad aggregation (double-counting in analytics), and ETL lag on the ingestion pipeline. Let's map owners, timelines, and any recurring pattern detection we can add.

sara: I'll collect the repro sets and link the postmortem doc + artifacts. filing tickets now (INF-3421 for spans, INF-3422 for aggregation). ETA EOD tomorrow to have repros. :memo:

liam: I can take the ETL lag. suspect the backfill window + small batch sizing on the kafka consumer. plan: bump batch window, tighten commit logic, add consumer lag monitor. target: PR by Thu, deploy Fri.

jessica: I'll own the aggregation fix — looks like two upstream services emitting the same metric with slightly different tags, and our aggregate job isn't deduping by trace_id. need a small test harness to validate. creating INF-3422, will propose schema change + dedupe step. aiming for next week.

randall: From infra/observability side: I'll add a dedicated alert for missing spans ratio > 0.5% over 5m and a dashboard row for aggregation anomalies (compare current vs rolling-24h delta). also adding a weekly smoke that runs a simple trace through the stack.

ops-bot: incident-bot: Incident #2027 closed 2027-03-12T18:10:00Z — summary: transient ETL lag + duplicate metric emissions. Linked: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3421, https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3422

omar: Action items consolidated: 1) INF-3421 (sara) repro + initial fix proposal — EOD tomorrow; 2) INF-3422 (jessica) aggregation dedupe PR — next Tue; 3) ETL lag (liam) PR Thu, deploy Fri; 4) randall to add alerts/dashboards + weekly smoke — done by next Wed. Can everyone confirm or update?

sara: confirm. I'll attach the sample payloads to the ticket and include a lightweight script to reproduce locally.

liam: confirm but flag: if batch window bump doesn't fully resolve, we may need a small partition rebalance which requires ops time. will call it out in the PR.

jessica: confirm. also requesting a small golden dataset from sara to validate dedupe logic before deployment.

randall: small note — adding alerts might flood on noisy environments; I'll implement a parrot alert that suppresses after repeated flaps and then route to a new "obs-aggregation" pager with low urgency.

omar: Good call on suppression. One more ask: can we add a simple recurring analytics job that detects 'aggregation drift' by comparing today's aggregates vs past 7-day median and auto-opens a ticket if delta > 12%? That would catch regressions before customers notice.

sara: I can prototype a query. starting point:

```
SELECT service_name, metric_name, COUNT(DISTINCT trace_id) as unique_traces
FROM spans_24h
WHERE ts >= now() - INTERVAL '24 hours'
GROUP BY 1,2
HAVING ABS(COUNT(DISTINCT trace_id) - median_7d) / NULLIF(median_7d,0) > 0.12;
```

sara: will wire that into a daily job and drop a link in INF-3422 once prototype passes.

liam: re: ETL monitoring, I'll add a small PromQL rule: `increase(kafka_consumer_lag[5m]) > 1000` and a graph. if we see > 5 such events in 24h, tag incident as recurring.

jessica: for aggregation dedupe I want to run a canary processing pipeline on a sample stream first — replicates the current aggregator but with dedupe enabled. if metric deltas are within 1% we roll.

randall: putting owners & deadlines into the postmortem doc now. also adding a checklist for rollback steps and who to call for immediate mitigation.

omar: Thanks — let's reconvene next Tuesday at 09:30 to validate fixes and close the loop. if anything slips, update the ticket and ping me. :thumbsup:
